title: Curvature-corrected CMOS bandgap reference (sub-1V, current-summing/Banba topology)
topology: Banba-style CMOS bandgap reference: two forward-biased parasitic pnp diodes (or diode-connected BJTs) driven at a fixed current ratio, with the PTAT and CTAT currents summed in the current domain (through resistors at the input of a self-biased current-mirror op-amp) rather than in the voltage domain. Summing currents instead of voltages lets the output reference voltage be set independently of the ~1.2V silicon bandgap voltage, enabling sub-1V supply operation.
spec_class: low-power PHY bias/reference — on-chip voltage/current reference for analog and mixed-signal PHY blocks (LDOs, ADC/DAC references, PLL charge pumps) where supply headroom is constrained below 1.8V core rails

pdk_portability.notes: sky130 exposes vertical parasitic PNP bipolar devices via the substrate (e.g. sky130_fd_pr__pnp_05v5) usable as the diode elements; absolute beta and saturation current vary by PDK and process corner, so PTAT/CTAT resistor ratios must be re-derived from PDK-specific device models rather than reused verbatim. The topology and current-summing method are portable to any PDK offering parasitic vertical BJTs or diode-connected devices.

sizing_approach: Set the diode area ratio (typically 1:8 to 1:24) to fix the PTAT delta-Vbe; size the CTAT/PTAT summing resistors so their current contributions cancel the first-order temperature dependence at the target output voltage (typically 0.5-0.6V, well below the ~1.2V bandgap voltage since summation happens in the current domain, not the voltage domain); iterate resistor ratios in simulation across process corners and -40C to 125C to trim the residual quadratic (curvature) term; add a curvature-correction branch (a resistor-diode network with a different temperature exponent) last and tune its weight to flatten the sub-1V output over temperature.
layout_idioms: common-centroid / cross-quad placement of the matched bipolar devices to cancel linear gradients across the die
resistor arrays laid out as unit-resistor strings with dummy elements at both ends, matched in orientation to cancel process-gradient mismatch
guard ring around the bipolar devices tied to substrate/well potential to collect injected minority carriers and isolate from adjacent digital switching noise
op-amp differential pair placed on an axis of symmetry with the current-summing node kept short and symmetric to the two resistor branches

source.citation: H. Banba, H. Shiga, A. Umezawa, T. Miyaba, T. Tanzawa, S. Atsumi, K. Sakui, "A CMOS bandgap reference circuit with sub-1-V operation," IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits, vol. 34, no. 5, pp. 670-674, May 1999.
source.license_or_openness: Peer-reviewed IEEE journal paper cited here for its topology and sizing methodology only (no figures or text reproduced), per the KB's open-sources sourcing rule. This is the foundational published reference for current-domain-summing sub-1V bandgap references; essentially all subsequent literature on the technique cites it directly.

notes: Most modern sub-1V bandgap variants, including curvature-corrected ones, build on this current-summing base circuit rather than replacing it. sky130's parasitic PNP devices are lower-performance than a dedicated BiCMOS process, so expect larger die area and more careful trimming to approach the temperature coefficient reported in the original paper.
